meta.titre: Defects of Vision: short sight, long sight, astigmatism, cataract and how each is corrected
meta.sous_theme: Causes and correction of eye defects

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Human Biology past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: Amina, a Form 5 student in Bamenda, has to sit at the front of the class to copy from the blackboard, yet she reads her textbook easily. Her cousin Ernest, who sells phone accessories in a Douala market, sees a distant bus number clearly but must hold a phone box at arm's length to read the small print. Both have a healthy eye in many ways, but light is not brought to a focus exactly on the retina. Examiners ask you to name the defect, say where the image forms, give the cause and state the lens or treatment that corrects it.

items: Light is refracted (bent) when it passes from air into the cornea and the lens of the eye.
A convex lens makes light rays converge, and a concave lens makes light rays spread out (diverge).
In a normal eye the cornea and lens focus light as a sharp image on the retina, which contains the light receptors.
The lens changes shape to focus on near and distant objects (accommodation).

sections.titre: Common defects of vision, their causes and corrections
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Normal and defective focusing

In a normal eye, light from an object is focused as a sharp image exactly on the retina. A defect of vision appears when the image falls in front of the retina, behind it, or is spread unevenly.

### The main defects

| Defect | What the person sees | Cause | Image forms | Correction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Short sight (myopia) | Near objects clear, distant objects blurred | Eyeball too long, or lens too strong (too curved) | In front of the retina | Concave (diverging) lens |
| Long sight (hypermetropia) | Distant objects clearer, near objects blurred | Eyeball too short, or lens too weak (too flat) | Behind the retina | Convex (converging) lens |
| Astigmatism | Parts of the picture blurred, lines in one direction less sharp | Cornea or lens not evenly curved | Different parts focused at different places | Cylindrical lens |
| Old sight (presbyopia) | Difficulty reading, usually after middle age | Lens becomes less elastic and cannot become thick enough | Behind the retina for near objects | Convex reading glasses |
| Cataract | Cloudy, misty vision | Lens becomes cloudy (opaque) | Light cannot pass through properly | Surgery to replace the lens |
| Colour blindness | Colours, often red and green, confused | Faulty or missing cones; inherited | Not a focusing fault | Cannot be corrected by lenses |

### How the correcting lens works

A short-sighted eye brings rays together too soon, so a concave lens spreads them slightly before they enter the eye and the focus moves back onto the retina. A long-sighted eye would bring rays together behind the retina, so a convex lens starts the bending earlier and moves the focus forward onto the retina. Spectacles, contact lenses and laser surgery on the cornea are different ways of correcting focusing faults.

variantes.nom: Short sight compared with long sight
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks you to compare the two defects or to say where the image forms.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Compare them under the same headings: what is seen clearly, cause (eyeball length or lens strength), position of the image relative to the retina, and the lens used. Short sight: image in front of the retina, concave lens. Long sight: image behind the retina, convex lens.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question mentions a cloudy lens, confusion of colours or poor sight in dim light.
variantes.contenu_markdown: A cataract is a cloudy lens, treated by surgery that replaces it. Colour blindness is inherited and caused by faulty cones, so no lens corrects it; it is more common in males because it is carried on the X chromosome as a recessive allele. Night blindness is poor sight in dim light and is caused by a lack of vitamin A in the diet.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks how eye defects and infections can be prevented.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Eat foods rich in vitamin A, such as liver, eggs, milk, carrots and dark green leaves. Do not read in very poor light, and wear a hat or sunglasses in very strong sunlight. Do not rub the eyes with dirty hands or share towels with a person with an eye infection, and have the eyes tested regularly.

sections.enonce_markdown: A boy can read a book held 20 cm from his face but cannot recognise the teacher standing at the far end of the football field. (a) Name his eye defect. (b) Give two possible causes. (c) State where the image of a distant object forms. (d) Name the lens that corrects the defect and say how it helps. *(6 marks)*

etapes.justification: Near objects are clear and distant objects are blurred, which identifies the defect.
The cause is always linked to the length of the eyeball or the strength of the lens.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The eyeball is too long, or the lens is too strong (too curved).

etapes.justification: The position of the image explains why the picture is blurred.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The image of a distant object forms **in front of the retina**, so it is out of focus when it reaches the retina.

etapes.action: Name the lens and explain its action.
etapes.justification: The correcting lens must move the focus back onto the retina.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A **concave (diverging) lens** spreads the rays slightly before they enter the eye, so they meet on the retina.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer.** (a) Short sight (myopia). (b) The eyeball is too long, or the lens is too strong. (c) In front of the retina. (d) A concave lens, which makes the rays diverge a little before they enter the eye, so the image is focused on the retina.

items.erreur_markdown: "Short sight is corrected with a convex lens."
items.pourquoi_faux: A convex lens increases the bending of light, which would make the focus fall even further in front of the retina.
items.correction_markdown: Short sight needs a **concave** lens; long sight needs a **convex** lens.

items.erreur_markdown: "In long sight the image forms in front of the retina."
items.pourquoi_faux: The eyeball is too short or the lens too weak, so the rays have not yet met when they reach the retina.
items.correction_markdown: In long sight the image forms **behind** the retina.

items.erreur_markdown: "A short-sighted person cannot see near objects."
items.pourquoi_faux: Short-sighted people see near objects clearly; it is distant objects that are blurred.
items.correction_markdown: Short sight: near clear, far blurred. Long sight: far clearer, near blurred.

items.erreur_markdown: "A cataract is treated with spectacles with a concave lens."
items.pourquoi_faux: A cataract is a cloudy lens. Glasses cannot make a cloudy lens transparent.
items.correction_markdown: The cloudy lens is removed by surgery and replaced by an artificial lens.

items.erreur_markdown: "Colour blindness is caused by damaged rods."
items.pourquoi_faux: Rods work in dim light and do not detect colour. Colour is detected by cones.
items.correction_markdown: Colour blindness is an inherited fault of the **cones**.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the eye defect or condition described in each case. (a) The eyeball is longer than normal. (b) The lens becomes cloudy. (c) The lens loses its elasticity with age and reading becomes difficult. (d) Red and green are confused. (e) State the lens used for the defect in (a).

Student X cannot read the blackboard from the back of the class but reads her exercise book easily. Student Y, also in Form 5, reads the blackboard but cannot read the small print of a newspaper held at normal reading distance. For each student name the defect, say where the image forms and name the lens that corrects it.
items.solution_markdown: **Student X:** short sight (myopia); the image forms in front of the retina; a concave lens corrects it. **Student Y:** long sight (hypermetropia); the image forms behind the retina; a convex lens corrects it.

items.enonce_markdown: An eye test was carried out on 480 students of a school. 72 were short-sighted, 36 were long-sighted and 12 were colour blind. Assume that no student had more than one of these conditions. (a) Calculate the percentage of students who were short-sighted. (b) How many students had none of the three conditions, and what percentage is this? (c) The short-sighted students were how many times as many as the long-sighted students? (d) Of the 12 colour-blind students, 11 were boys. Explain why colour blindness is more common in boys than in girls.
items.solution_markdown: (a) $\frac{72}{480} \times 100 = 15$, so **15 %**. (b) Students with a condition: $72 + 36 + 12 = 120$. Students with none: $480 - 120 = 360$, which is $\frac{360}{480} \times 100 = 75$, so **360 students (75 %)**. (c) $\frac{72}{36} = 2$, so **twice as many**. (d) The gene for colour blindness is on the X chromosome and is recessive. A boy (XY) has only one X chromosome, so one faulty allele is enough to make him colour blind. A girl (XX) must inherit the faulty allele on both X chromosomes, which is less likely.

items_markdown: Short sight: image in front of the retina (eyeball too long or lens too strong); corrected with a concave lens.
Long sight: image behind the retina (eyeball too short or lens too weak); corrected with a convex lens.
Astigmatism is uneven curvature of the cornea or lens; old sight is loss of lens elasticity with age.
Cataract (cloudy lens) needs surgery; colour blindness (faulty cones) is inherited and not corrected by lenses.
For any defect, give four things: symptom, cause, position of the image, correction.
